title: My BTC bot beat plain DCA in the backtest. Live, it tied. The exits were the real problem.
author: Bright_Clerk1452

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 'if a human overrides the bot you're grading the human' is the line most people never get to. and the exits result is the normal one: a DCA bot with a stop is two strategies, and the sell half gets judged against holding, which in BTC's case is a brutal benchmark. the buy signals were never where the money was.

replies.author: Bright_Clerk1452
replies.body:
yeah, splitting it into two strategies is the right way to see it. the buy side barely mattered: signal-weighted buying tied plain DCA within a fraction of a percent. all the damage came from the sell side, and you’re right that “vs just holding BTC” is about as unforgiving a benchmark as exists.

the human override part is what surprised me most. once someone sells by hand for their own reasons, the record stops measuring the strategy and starts measuring the person. which makes me think any honest track record has to log overrides as their own events, not blend them in.

curious if you’ve seen anyone handle that well, bots or signal groups that separate “what the system did” from “what the person did”?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the clean follow-up is running plain DCA and DCA-with-your-exits on the same window and reading only the gap, since the buy signal tied anyway. my guess from the numbers you posted is the stop did most of the damage on the deep dips, which is exactly where holding wins in BTC.
